symbols.remarks: Resume build options of `rivet({ resume })`: modules, entry, chunk grouping and preload.

members.name: appModules
members.doc:
Every app `.tsx`/`.jsx` module (inside the Vite root, outside `node_modules`) compiles in resume mode
when something resumable imports it, like source-package modules; `resume.modules` then only seeds the
graph. Without it a component module not listed in `modules` is silently non-resumable and the page
fails at request time ("Resume manifest has no chunk").
`rivetRouter` sets it (default true there); plain `rivet({ resume })` keeps the explicit list.

members.name: cap
members.doc:
Most shared chunks one entry (a symbol chunk; with `chunks: "route"` a route's chunk) may load after merging
(ROUTE-CHUNKS cluster 2026-10-18): an entry over the cap keeps merging the cheapest pair of its shared chunks past
the budget, pinned chunks and import order still respected. Applies to the bundler's shared code chunks and, in
route mode, to the shared symbol chunks. Unset = the budget alone decides.

members.name: chunks
members.doc:
Chunk grouping: "route" (default since 2026-10-18, derived-client plan M1) one chunk per lazy-import target's
static module graph (`lazyComponent` / route imports), a main chunk, and the modules several routes reach
placed by the bundler into shared chunks (merged under `merge` / `cap`); "component" one chunk per component;
"group" one chunk per `<ChunkGroup>` subtree (components rendered in several groups, or none, keep their own
chunk). Chunks of the same group / route prefetch each other once one is used. Measured (ui-docs frames, Slow 4G):
route needs a quarter of the files of component through the first click for about a fifth more bytes, and
the first click downloads nothing. Route mode splits each route chunk by load class: a module whose every symbol
loads on intent / interaction (component-level `preload`, else a `preload.rules` rule) goes to the route's intent
chunk (`resume-<route>-intent`, same sibling group), so a page booting its route chunk (an idle effect, a boot-time
listener) does not evaluate it, and the page fetch-ahead leaves it to its intent prefetch.

members.name: dev
members.doc:
Dev server: serve the modules resumable (`rivetRouter` sets it unless `dev: { resume: false }`).
Client modules compile in resume mode (which adds the export list of locals symbol chunks import)
and `<module>?rivet-chunk=<Component>` serves a component's symbol chunk, compiled like a
production chunk (`api.devResume.manifest()` points symbols at them). Default false: dev client
modules compile without resume mode (their pages client-render).

members.name: domData
members.doc:
DOM-backed loader data (DOM-DATA; spec `docs/design/specs/2026-10-20-dom-backed-loader-data-design.md`):
plain JSON data the page renders as an element's whole text (`<dd>{row().name}</dd>`: loader rows, `<For>` items) is
not written into `rivet/state` again — the browser reads those strings back from the DOM on first access (at the latest
at the first idle after resume). Adds the reader (`@rivetjs/runtime` `dom-resume-data.ts`, about 1.8 KB min / 0.6 KB br)
to the build's resume runtime, the registry + `D` encoder (`server-dom-data.ts`, about 9.1 KB min) to its server and
`domData: true` to the resume manifest; servers write `D` entries only then. Default true (LAZY-FLIP); `false`
builds carry neither. Unset, a build whose resume modules have no structural `<For>` carries neither too; `true` keeps them.
With `model: "derived"` (DERIVED-C5) it is off unless set to `true`: `<For>` items of a record's data props become
tail `d` entries the derived client reads back from the rows (`DOM_DATA` in `dom-derived.ts`; no `dom-data-resume` /
server registry).

members.name: entry
members.doc: Root-relative resume entry whose default export is `createResume(...)`; defaults to an empty one.

members.name: lazy
members.doc:
When a chunk's lazy imports (lazy routes/components it may load on use) prefetch: "idle" (default)
once an eager/idle/visible chunk is scheduled, or "intent" only, with the chunk's own intent prefetch.

members.name: lazyOwned
members.doc:
Root-relative modules that prefetch their own lazy imports (the router's generated App: its intent
handler loads the hovered route's page): their dynamic imports are never listed as lazies of the chunk
holding them (nor of any chunk, when only they import the target), so a page's resume state does not name
every route chunk and intent on the App's chunk does not prefetch every page.

members.name: lazyRows
members.doc:
Lazy collection rows (LAZY-ROWS; spec `docs/design/specs/2026-10-19-lazy-collection-rows-design.md`):
the browser runtime of this build can materialise lazy `<For>` rows (state `L`: rows rendered without resume
records, materialised on their first event / a read signal's first change). Adds the lazy rows runtime (about
a chunk of its own: `@rivetjs/runtime` `dom-resume-lazy.ts` + `dom-adopt-run.ts`, loaded only by pages whose state holds
`L` entries, preloaded by their lazy add-on — LAZY-BLOCKERS; plus the adopt-run hooks of the DOM runtime and the resume
runtime's lazy hooks in the entry, zero-cost `dom` + `dom-resume` `[lazyRows]` lines) to the build and the chunk's URL
as `lazyRows` to the resume manifest (dev: `true`); builds with `false` carry none of it (0 bytes). The server writes lazy
row records when the manifest says so, unless its environment has `RIVET_LAZY_ROWS=off` (read per render): build once,
toggle the variable to A/B. Default true (LAZY-FLIP); `false` leaves the runtime and the manifest flag out. Unset, a build
whose resume modules have no lazy-eligible keyed `<For>` (compile `forRows`) leaves them out too; `true` keeps them.

members.name: merge
members.doc:
Shared chunk merging (client build, PRELOAD-GROUP 2026-10-12): the bundler splits shared code into one chunk per
distinct set of entries using it, so a page's preload closure is dozens of small files. Shared modules that load
together merge into one chunk while the source bytes entries (symbol chunks, lazily imported modules, app entry,
runtime) load without needing them stay under this budget per request saved — summed over entries and checked per
merge, so the budget is amortised: one entry can pay more (`chunk-groups.ts`). Chunks every page loads never take
page code; a merged chunk never closes an import cycle. Default 65536 (`MERGE_BUDGET`; 2048 until 2026-10-18: 64 K cut the
files of a page by a third to a half at flat bytes on the ui-docs frames); `false` = the bundler's automatic split.
Skipped when the build sets `codeSplitting: false`, `manualChunks` or `advancedChunks`.

members.name: model
members.doc:
Resume model (experimental; derived client, spec `docs/design/specs/2026-10-18-structural-resume-design.md` §3.3–3.5,
plan `docs/design/plans/2026-10-18-derived-client.md` M2). `"serialized"` (default): today's records + state table +
symbol chunks. `"derived"`: resume modules compile with `resume: { model: "derived" }` on both targets (boundary
verdicts from the build's facts fixpoint, `facts-fixpoint.ts`), the page ships values only (a boundaries tail) and the
browser adopts boundaries over the server nodes. The build serves the lazy rows + `DERIVED` runtime switches, emits one
chunk per module holding boundaries plus the runtime entry (default export of `@rivetjs/runtime/dom-derived`), and
writes the manifest with `model: "derived"`, `runtime` and `symbols` keyed by boundary name (`<module>#<Name>`); the
router renders such builds with `renderDerived`. `chunks` / `merge` / `cap` / `preload` / `lazy` / `entry` /
`lazyRows` do not apply; `domData` applies to list rows (DERIVED-C5: tail `d`, read back by `dom-derived.ts`). Dev: an
edit of a resume module reloads the page.

members.name: modules
members.doc: Root-relative source modules compiled in resume mode.

members.name: preload
members.doc:
Preload overrides. Automatic: click/submit/input handlers prefetch on intent; handlers repeated on
3+ elements (list rows) and hover-like events when visible; window/document client events at idle;
`passive: false` listeners eagerly. First matching rule wins; a string matches a symbol id prefix
(`src/page.tsx#Component`). Precedence: element `preload="…"` directive > component level (module
`export const preload = "…"`, or a `<ChunkGroup preload>`) > these rules > automatic. With `chunks: "route"`, a
module whose symbols all resolve to `intent` / `interaction` here (or at the component level) moves to its route's
intent chunk and out of the page's fetch-ahead (`data-fo`); rule the renderers of such components too (a frame whose
child slots render a menu imports the menu's module).

data, whatever its call sites pass or which contexts it reads), like a route module's default export. `rivetRouter()`
adds its generated `app.tsx` (`Root`: the route payload as props, M2 R5).

members.name: adapter
members.doc:

entry (client manifests inlined, dependencies bundled). `"fetch"`: `dist/server/fetch.js`
(`export default { fetch }`, any web-standard runtime). Platforms, packaged after the server build:
`"vercel"` (`.vercel/output`, Build Output API v3), `"netlify"` (`.netlify/v1` + `dist/netlify`),

`"deno"` (`dist/server/deno.js`).

members.doc: Route announcer for screen readers after client navigation (default true; `false` opts out).

members.name: base
members.doc:

Route patterns, `<Link to>`, `navigate()`, data requests, prefetch and the adapters follow it.

members.name: bridges
members.doc:
Framework bridges (`rivet({ bridges })`: `react()` from `@rivetjs/bridge-react/vite`, `preact()` from
`@rivetjs/bridge-preact/vite`, …): those frameworks' components render as islands inside the routed pages.
Server / static modes only.

members.name: clientRouter
members.doc:
Client-side navigation on pages with nothing else to resume (opt-in, Astro's `<ClientRouter />` model).
`true`: every page ships the router (link clicks / intent prefetch / back-forward served in place).
`false` (default): the router's listeners alone do not make a page resumable — a page without resumable
symbols, client effects or forms ships zero JS (no loader, state script or modulepreloads) and its
links load documents; pages that resume anyway still route in place. Ignored in `csr` (always routed).

members.name: css
members.doc: Scoped styles options passed to `rivet({ css })`.

members.name: dev
members.doc:
Dev server. `resume` (default true): pages resume like production (recorder state, inline loader,
symbol chunks served by Vite); the first hot update switches the page to client rendering, after
which components hot-replace in place. `false`: pages client-render over the server HTML (the
recorder still runs, so serialization errors still reach the overlay).

members.name: devtools
members.doc: DevTools on the dev server when `@rivetjs/devtools` is installed (default true; see `rivet()`).

members.name: document
members.doc: Root-relative module whose default export is the `DocumentShell` (default `src/document.ts`).

members.name: forms
members.doc:
The app uses `@rivetjs/forms` (directly or through `@rivetjs/ui` `Form`): enhanced submits reach the router
through `Symbol.for("rivet.router")` (implies `navigate`). Default: detected (`routerUsage`).

members.name: head
members.doc:
Component head (`@rivetjs/kit` `<Title>`, `<Meta>`, …): `components` holds each page's document
start until its shell rendered; on by default when the kit Vite plugin (`kit()`) is installed.
`early` keeps route `head` exports only (document start written first).

members.name: images
members.doc: `?image` / `?jsx` imports (`rivet({ images })`); build with the app builder so server-only images reach the client output.

members.name: inlineStylesheets
members.doc:
Stylesheets written into the page as `<style>` instead of linked (Astro's `build.inlineStylesheets`), production
server / static pages, decided per page. `"auto"` (default): all of the page's sheets (global + route) when their
brotli sizes add up to at most 6 KB (the page then has no render-blocking stylesheet request), else each sheet of
at most Vite's `build.assetsInlineLimit` (4096 raw bytes; a function limit counts as 4096). `{ maxTotalBrotli }`:
`auto` with another total (bytes). `"always"`: every sheet; `"never"`: all linked. Sheets with relative `url()` /
`@import` references stay linked. Inline styles carry the page's CSP nonce (static pages: hashed into a
`style-src` you set).

members.name: mode
members.doc: `server` (default) and `static` resume server-rendered pages; `csr` mounts a single-page app.

members.name: navigate
members.doc: The app calls `navigate()` / `invalidate()` / `revalidate()` / `setSearchParams()`. Default: detected (`routerUsage`).

members.name: outDir

members.name: params

members.name: prefetch
members.doc:
Document prefetch for navigations that load a document (`@rivetjs/router/prefetch`): every page's
head gets Speculation Rules (Chromium) + a ~1 kB inline intent fallback. `"document"` / `"prerender"`:
also the default for every same-origin link without its own `prefetch` / `data-rivet-prefetch`
(plain `<a>` included; `"none"` opts one out). `true`: only links marked `prefetch="document"` /
`"prerender"`. Default: detected (`routerUsage`: such a mark in the sources); `false`: off.
Server / static modes (ignored in `csr`).

members.name: prefetchEagerness
members.doc:
When Chromium starts a document prefetch / prerender (Speculation Rules `eagerness`):
`"conservative"` (pointer / touch down), `"moderate"` (default: also a ~200 ms hover), `"eager"`
(sooner). Applies only while `prefetch` is on; the fallback keeps its 65 ms / focus / down timing.

members.name: prefetchPaths
members.doc:

`rel=external` links and links whose path no route matches (every page carries the route-path RegExp, in the
Speculation Rules and in the fallback call). `false`: only `data-rivet-reload` / `rel=external` links — for apps
whose document links all carry `reload` (the docs sites: −7.7 KB of route patterns per page).

members.name: preload
members.doc:

`background` = byte budget (minified closures) of below-the-fold `visible` chunks also prefetched at idle; `0` off.
Default 1 MiB. Dev pages keep `visible` chunks viewport-only (dev manifests have no bundle sizes).

members.name: resume

members.name: routeRules
members.doc:

stored in process (fresh for `maxAge` s, then served stale while one render refreshes them; `isr: true` until
`revalidate()`), with ETag / Last-Modified → 304 and `s-maxage` / `stale-while-revalidate` for CDNs. JSON data:
the server entry exports it, every adapter applies it (`createApp` / adapter `routeRules` replace it). Dev applies
`headers` only. See `@rivetjs/router/route-cache`.

members.name: routes
members.doc: Routes directory, root-relative (default `src/routes`).

members.name: searchParams
members.doc:
The app reads search params (`useSearchParams()` / `SearchParams`): the server provides the
request's, the resume entry the browser's. Default: detected from the project's sources
(`routerUsage`); set `true` when only a published dependency reads them.

members.name: serverOnly
members.doc:
Server-only modules besides `*.server.*` files and modules importing `@rivetjs/router/server-only`: module ids /
specifiers or RegExps (virtual modules serving server data, e.g. `"virtual:docs/api"`; plugins declare theirs as
`api.rivetServerOnly`, `rivet({ serverOnly })` too). Before each build / dev start the router walks every route's
browser graph: a page route reaching one through its own module and plain helper modules is a document route (links
load its document, its module leaves the client build); a component module, layout or error page reaching one fails
the build (RV3011, with the import chain and the routes). `{ modules, reach: "warn" }`: components reaching one only
warn, and the pages rendering them become document routes. Server / static modes (csr keeps the import error).

members.name: staticIcons

members.name: styles
members.doc: Root-relative stylesheets: client build inputs, linked by the document (`styles`).

members.name: trailingSlash
members.doc:
Trailing-slash policy. `"ignore"` (default): `/a` and `/a/` serve the same page as requested.
`"never"` / `"always"`: one canonical form — page GET/HEAD requests for the other answer 308,
`<Link>` / `navigate()` write hrefs in it, the static adapter writes `a.html` (`never`) or
`a/index.html`. `/` itself never changes; endpoints and other methods are never redirected.

members.name: transitions
members.doc:
Route transitions (View Transitions) + pending UI. Off by default; `true` = defaults. The
transitions module loads on the first navigation intent; the generated resume entry provides
the navigation context (a custom `resume.entry` must add `[Navigation, navigation]` itself).

members.doc: Pending bytes (`offset - start`) at which a write flushes; 0 flushes every write (a full queue).

members.name: claim
members.doc:
Raw-slab protocol: make room for `length` (≤ 32 KiB) bytes at `bytes[offset]`. The renderer writes a
whole compiled record / list row there, then hands the end offset to `commit`. Returns a wait under
backpressure.

members.name: commit
members.doc: Records bytes written in place after `claim`; flushes past the threshold.

members.name: flush
members.doc: Hands off `start..offset`; returns a wait under backpressure.

members.name: oversize
members.doc: Writes a byte chunk larger than `size` (pending bytes already flushed).

members.name: renew
members.doc: Continues in a slab with at least `size` bytes of room (`start = offset = 0`).

members.name: reserve
members.doc: After a flush: a fresh slab when the room left cannot hold `size` bytes.

members.name: schedule
members.doc: Arms a deferred flush (only called while `scheduled` is false).

members.name: write
members.doc: Encodes a string chunk; returns a promise only under backpressure.

members.name: writeBytes
members.doc: Copies pre-encoded UTF-8 bytes; same backpressure contract as write().

members.name: writeInteger
members.doc: Writes a safe integer as ASCII digits (exactly String(value)): digit pairs for int32, `write` past it.

members.name: writeText
members.doc:
Writes `text` HTML-text-escaped (`&` `<` `>`, as escapeText) in one pass: short strings are escaped

members.doc:
Resume model (plan `docs/design/plans/2026-10-18-derived-client.md` M2). `serialized` (default): the recorder below
(records, state table, loader). `derived`: modules compiled with `resume: { model: "derived" }` call only the boundary
recorder (`@rivetjs/runtime/server-derived`: `_rB` / `_rBOut` / `_rBEnd` / `_rBAttr` / `_rSig` / `_rSigStore`; a render
with `model: "derived"` before that module loaded renders as the plain server target — no boundary, no tail); the tail is one
`<script type="rivet/boundaries">` of values (boundary records + keyed state + wake lists), no state table / loader
unless a serialized-model record was made too (`.ts` helpers calling `_r*` directly). `For` rows and `Show` /
`Switch` branches keep their `<!--rN[-->…<!--]-->` markers; out-of-order streaming is not entered (no site scopes).

members.name: nonce
members.doc: CSP nonce for the inline loader (and stream) scripts.

members.name: origin
members.doc:
The request's origin: same-origin `URL` values in the state serialize relative to it (the browser resolves them
against its location), so a prerendered page's state carries no build-time origin (`http://localhost`).

members.name: preload
members.signature: preload?: { ahead?: boolean; background?: number; lean?: boolean }
members.doc:
Preload planner. `background`: byte budget (minified, manifest `sizes`) of the static closures of `visible` chunks
that are also prefetched in the background at idle, in plan order; chunks past it wait for the viewport. Default
1 MiB (`BACKGROUND_DEFAULT`); `0` turns background prefetch off (embedded frames, pages with many demos).
`lean`: nothing loads before an interaction — no scheduled prefetch (eager / idle / visible / background, as the
loader does under Save-Data) and no fetch-ahead of a lazy router's chunks; handlers load on intent / interaction.
`ahead`: fetch-ahead (`data-fo`: low-priority modulepreloads after `load`, the web fonts and an idle slice; fetched,
never evaluated) on two kinds of page: bridge D-lean pages (`DeferredState`) keep the fetch-ahead of the runtime +
lazy router chunks, so the first link click does not wait for the runtime; on `resume.chunks: "route"` builds
(manifest `fetchAhead`) every page also fetches its own handler chunks + their static closures, so the first
interaction downloads nothing. Ignored with `lean` and on every other page. The router sets it while the app has
document prefetch on (`rivetRouter({ prefetch })`).

The build's browser runtime reads DOM-backed loader data (`rivet({ resume })` default since LAZY-FLIP, DOM-DATA): plain

members.name: lazyRows
members.doc:
The build's browser runtime materialises lazy collection rows (`rivet({ resume })` default since LAZY-FLIP; LAZY-T5B):

(`data-lz`) at the first event walk, with the runtime.
